messages.author: b23750489f41fd4c
messages.subject: TITAN CNA - Allele Counts
parts:
Hello,
I am following the steps posted in (http://compbio.bccrc.ca/software/titan/titan-running-titancna/) to analyze my TN paired exome data and I had a question regarding the allele counts generated with samtools:

samtools mpileup -uv -I -f ref.fasta -r $chrToUse -l dbSNP.positions.txt norm.bam | bcftools call -v -c - | grep -e "#" -e "0/1" > normHetSNPs.vcf


I notice that for the exomes, a very large proportion of these sites have very low DP (1-5 ) and are predominantly present in intronic or intergenic regions. Is this taken into consideration during the analysis? Does the inclusion of the "targetedSequence =exons" flag in the correctReadDepth call correct for this? 

cnData <- correctReadDepth(tumWig,normWig,gc,map, targetedSequence = exons)

If not, I was wondering if I should pre-filter the allele counts output before proceeding with the pipeline.

thanks
Arun

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: TITAN CNA - Allele Counts
parts:
Hi Arun,

You are correct.  That line in R, when invoking correctReadDepth, if you specify a bed file containing your exons, then it will account for the non-coding bins.  Typically, this bed file is the interval file corresponding to your hybrid-capture bait set.

Then, when you find the overlap of the HET sites with the log ratio bins, the sites within non-coding regions will be excluded
logR <- getPositionOverlap(data$chr,data$posn,cnData)
data$logR <- log(2^logR)

Hope this helps.

Best,
Gavin

messages.author: b23750489f41fd4c
messages.subject: Re: TITAN CNA - Allele Counts
parts:
Hi Gavin,
Perfect! Thanks for your quick response. 

One additional question. Would you recommend any other parameter modifications for exome based calling? I am noticing that an expected copy number change is not being picked up by TITAN-CNA in two of the samples (they are all at least 150-200x coverage) and am not sure how to go about changing the following parameters to best influence exome based CNA calls.

  • maxiter = maximum number of EM iterations allowed. In practice, it does not exceed 20.
  • maxiterUpdate = maximum number of coordinate descent iterations during the M-step when parameters are estimated
  • txnExpLen = influences prior probability of genotype transitions in the HMM. The larger the value, the lower tendency to change state; however, too small and it produces underflow problems.  ## in version v1.2.0, underflow will not occur ##
  • txnZstrength = influences prior probability of clonal cluster transitions in the HMM. Larger values means lower tendency to change clonal cluster state.
  • useOutlierState = logical indicating whether an additional outlier state should be used. In practice, this usually is not necessary.
  • normalEstimateMethod = specifies how to handle normal proportion estimation. To estimate, use “map” which is maximum a posteriori. If you wish to not estimate this parameter, then use “fixed”. This will default the normal proportion to whatever is specified in “params$normalParams$n_0″. For example, if you know that this sample has absolutely no normal contamination, then use params$normalParams$n_0 <- 0 and set normalEstimateMethod=”fixed”.
  • estimateS = logical indicating whether to account for clonality and estimate subclonal events
  • estimatePloidy = logical indicating whether to estimate and account for tumour ploidy
thanks
Arun

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: TITAN CNA - Allele Counts
parts:
Hi Arun,

First, I'd like to point you to an R script that I have provided your convenience.  
https://github.com/gavinha/TitanCNA-utils

Given the input files, this script will run R component of the analysis, generate all output files including plots.  It also has some settings specific for exome analysis.

In general, you can decrease txnExpLen and that will lead to more segments.  Essentially, this governors the self-state-transition probabilities.  

Best,
Gavin

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: TITAN CNA - Allele Counts
parts:
Hi Arun,

Please use "--hetFile" instead of "--hetfile"

The "cnFile" argument requires the corrected log ratio coverage files.  It is not the TITAN output files.  This script will generate all the TITAN results.
You can generate this log ratio file as before using this command:

Save cnData to a file and use this for the argument.
The reason the log ratio file should be separate from the script is because there is a random sampling step in the normalization that produces slightly different results if you have more than 50k data points.  To ensure reproducibility, it is best to generate this file outside of the main R script.  This way, you can modify TitanCNA-specific parameters knowing that you have the identical inputs for each run.

Also, you need be using TitanCNA v1.10.1 or greater.  Please use the latest version of R/Bioconductor to make sure it has the latest version or simply download the latest version from GitHub:
https://github.com/gavinha/TitanCNA/releases/tag/v1.13.1

Best,
Gavin
